newsitem.title: UK: UK manufacturing boosted by domestic demand - IFS.
newsitem.headline: UK manufacturing boosted by domestic demand - IFS.

text.p: British manufacturers continued to enjoy buoyant business conditions in the latest quarter thanks to the strength of domestic demand, the Institute of Directors said on Monday.

The IoD's latest business opinion survey, which canvassed 503 members between June 2 and 13, showed manufacturers enjoyed stronger growth in output, reflecting a large increase in domestic order books.

Business optimism, company performance and growth in employment, were little changed from the March survey. The IoD said business services remains the most buoyant sector but saw much less evidence of a "two-tier economy" than in previous results.

"I have to say we are surprised by the strength of the responses from manufacturing this time, which suggest that rising home demand has outweighed any adverse effect from the appreciation of sterling," said Stephen Davies, the IoD's economic research executive.
"Sterling has, however, appreciated by more than four percent since the survey was conducted, so exporters would certainly be less optimistic now than when they were interviewed," Davies said.
The pound, up more than 30 percent against the mark in the last year, has rocketed again in recent weeks, climbing from 2.84 at the end of the IoD survey period, to stand above three marks on Monday.
The survey said there remains a clear contrast in price pressures between services, where prices are rising, and manufacturing and distributions, where prices are falling.
Overall, fewer companies this quarter said they had increased prices while slightly more firms reported higher costs. Pay settlements edged up.
